summary: Big-O notation describes how the number of steps an algorithm takes grows with the input size n. This program counts steps for O(n), O(log n), and O(n^2) code at three sizes.
notes: steps += 1 inside each loop counts work directly, so the table is the same on every computer.
When n grows 10 times, linear_search grows 10 times, binary_search grows by only about 3 steps, and count_pairs grows 100 times.
time.perf_counter() measures real time, but the numbers change on every run and depend on the machine.
pitfall: Running binary_search on an unsorted list gives no error. It just returns wrong answers, because the halving rule assumes items[mid] < target means the target is to the right.
